title: Hedge funds cut tech stocks at record pace, Goldman says

Hedge funds cut tech stocks at record pace, Goldman says

Trade GS on Coinbase

Investing.com -- Hedge funds reduced their technology stock positions at the fastest rate in at least a decade during the five trading sessions through Oct. 15, according to data from Goldman Sachs Inc.'s prime desk.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

The selling came as global technology shares declined sharply. The Nasdaq 100 dropped 5.5% for its worst performance since April 2025 last week as the AI trade unwound globally. Technology was the worst-performing sector in the MSCI World Index during the period covered by Goldman Sachs's data.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

Gross trading activity among hedge funds fell at the fastest pace in nearly three months, according to a note by Goldman's global banking and markets group.

Global equities were net sold at two standard deviations against the past year's flows, the data showed. Information technology led the selling by a wide margin, with the largest reduction in gross positions in two months. Semiconductors took the biggest dollar loss.

Hedge funds still maintain large technology holdings. Net allocation to the sector stands at 23.5% of the global Prime book, which remains in the 90th percentile versus the past five years, the note said.

The funds have become more cautious in their positioning. Their net leverage, which measures how much long positions outweigh short positions, fell to a one-year low of 48.6%.
